answer.answer:
Improving site safety with robotics rests, on the evidence here, on one asserted causal route: moving work off site into prefabrication. Everything else that bears on safety comes in as a condition on human-robot collaboration rather than as a direct route to safer sites: compliance with robot safety standards, workforce training, and power-and-force-limited collaborative operation to keep contact forces within biomechanical limits. Safety is already the stated reason for adopting several deployed processes, including digging and material handling at readiness level 8 and structural-core drilling at readiness level 7, though none of those deployed records is tied in the material in front of me to the site-safety value itself. Watch the price of the prefabrication route: it depends on precise up-front planning and logistics and on third-party certification and traceability, so the safety gain is bought with front-loaded design and compliance effort.

**The one asserted route to site safety**

Improve site safety (VA13) is a Value enabler that applies in the Structural Construction phase in a value-realizing role [1], and it is activated in 39 of the 50 coded cases [2], making it one of the most widely realised values in the coded record. Its dependency structure is thin and can be quoted exactly: VA13 carries 1 inbound and 0 outbound dependency edges [2]. That single inbound edge is DEP19: Prefabrication/off-site (PR2) enables Improve site safety (VA13), on the reasoning that moving work offsite improves site safety [3], backed by peer-reviewed evidence [2]. So within this graph, prefabrication is the only thing asserted to produce site safety; everything else associated with VA13 is correlation, not a claimed cause.

**What the prefabrication route itself requires**

Prefabrication/off-site (PR2) is activated in 20 of the 50 coded cases [2] and carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all of them listed in the context [2]. Its preconditions are the work you have to do to get the safety benefit:

- PR2 dependsOn RI14: prefabrication relies on precise up-front planning and logistics [2] [1].
- PR2 dependsOn RI18: a functional regulatory system for offsite compliance requires third-party certification and traceability [2] [1].
- Routes in: DfMA (PR9) orients the project toward offsite manufacture, and early involvement of the delivering production party (CO11) is required to integrate manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design [2], and supply chain integration (VA14) supports the offsite production line [2].

The same move also carries non-safety returns: PR2 enables schedule compression (VA2), quality from the controlled factory environment (VA3), and improved quality control with reduced errors and rework (VA10) [2].

**Keeping people safe where robots and workers share the work**

Human-robot interaction (CO6) is activated in 32 of the 50 coded cases and carries 0 inbound and 3 outbound dependency edges [2], all three of which are safety-relevant, though none of them targets VA13 directly:

- CO6 mitigates RI20: power-and-force-limiting collaborative operation within biomechanical limits mitigates contact-injury risk [2], on standards evidence [1].
- CO6 dependsOn RI18: human-robot collaborative work depends on compliance with robot safety standards [2] [1].
- CO6 dependsOn RI6: the success of human-robot collaboration is contingent on a skilled workforce, so it depends on addressing workforce training [2] [1].

Correlationally, CO6 co-occurs with Improve site safety (VA13) at weight 28, and more strongly with Improve human wellbeing (VA16, weight 30), Reduce human dependency (VA1, weight 32) and Significant human involvement (RE6, weight 32) [4]. These are statistical associations across cases, not directional claims.

**Controlling the environment**

A separate, sparsely used route is environmental control. On-site digital fabrication (PR8) hasPrecondition CO12: environments need to be much more structured and controlled before construction robots can take over [2], and the all-weather cover lets welding and assembly proceed normally even in rain, while the climbing all-weather roof with overhead delivery increases productivity and stabilises process and quality [2]. Note the adoption reality: CO12 is activated in 1 of the 50 coded cases [2]. Note also that the stated benefits of CO12 in the context are productivity, process and quality, not safety.

**The robotics side of the question**

Of the robotics enablers retrieval reached, only the robot arm carries a dependency edge: RE2 enables Robotic assembly (PR4) [2], with PR4 dependsOn RE2 [2] reciprocally, and RE2 carries 1 inbound and 1 outbound edge and is activated in 22 of the 50 coded cases [2]. Mobile (AT9) is activated in 28 of the 50 coded cases [2] and enables on-site digital fabrication through autonomous repositioning and localisation [2], which loops back to the CO12 precondition above. One constraint worth planning around indoors: RI5 constrains PR12, since reliable GNSS signals are typically unavailable indoors, constraining localisation method choice [2]. None of these robotics enablers has an asserted edge to VA13.

**Deployed record**

Three deployed processes in the context name safety as an adoption driver. Process census_RXM4-5 was adopted to address safety and labor, performs digging and material handling on sitework, substructure and foundation, at technology readiness level 8 [5]. Process census_RXM1-3 was adopted to address safety and market, performs digging and material handling on sitework, at technology readiness level 8 [6]. Process census_RXM23-1 was adopted to address safety, performs drilling, and works on the structural core and sitework, at technology readiness level 7 [7]. The context gives no firm for any of these three, and it does not link any of them to VA13 as an activated enabler, so they evidence safety as a motive for deployment, not a measured safety outcome.

**Reading the limits**

The exact edge counts licence one closed claim only: prefabrication is the sole asserted inbound dependency to site safety. The co-occurrence lists are explicitly a cut, 1898 co-occurrence edges touch these enablers and only the 15 strongest are shown [2], and PR15 and CO6 each have over 120 co-occurring enablers in total [8] [4], so nothing about the absence of a safety measure from these lists means it is absent from the record. The widening of "robotics" to include the unmanned mobile vehicle and gantry-type systems does not add a safety path: no dependency edge for those reaches VA13 in the material here.
